title: Woman yelled at police not to shoot Dustyhorn, coroner's inquest hears
article: A coroner's inquest into a deadly police shooting in Saskatoon is hearing about the incident from a new perspective.
On Tuesday, Lori Worm testified about what she saw on the night Dwayne Dustyhorn was shot five times by police, who said they were responding to a domestic dispute.

Worm began her testimony by frankly admitting that her relationship with Dustyhorn was a stormy one. In 2007, Dustyhorn had been charged with assaulting Worm. As that matter was before the courts, he was under orders to stay away from her.
Despite that, the two reconciled, albeit only briefly.
On the same day that they got back together, Dec. 22, 2007, Worm said they were fighting again. She said the two of them had been drinking heavily.
Dustyhorn, she told the jury, was expressing concern about the prospect of going to jail over the assault charge.
In Worm's recounting of events, she said it was Dustyhorn who made a call to 911 and quickly hung up.
She said he then grabbed two kitchen knives and taped them to his hands. Worm said she warned him that his actions were dangerous.
"The cops will shoot you!" Worm recalled telling Dustyhorn, but she said he ignored her.
Her recollection of the encounter with the police officers who did arrive, around 3:00 a.m., was sketchy. But she told the inquest that she did not fear for her life.
She said there was a brief struggle as she tried to wrest the knives from Dustyhorn. Worm also recalled screaming at police not to shoot.
However, Dustyhorn charged at officers, and they fired.
The jurors had already heard evidence that Dustyhorn was struck by five bullets and died at the scene.
The inquest is scheduled to run until Friday.
Dustyhorn was 38 at the time of his death.
